findings.title: Referer-based host check is spoofable and uses blank URI check incorrectly
findings.body: `ensure_embeddable` relies solely on `request.referer` to validate the embedding host, comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The HTTP Referer header is client-controlled and can be spoofed or omitted by proxies/browsers, so this is a weak access control mechanism for an endpoint that creates topics indirectly via jobs. There is no additional check (e.g. a signed token, Origin header validation with stricter rules, or CORS) protecting this. Also, when `embed_url` differs in scheme/case from `embeddable_host`, no normalization occurs, which could lead to false negatives/positives.

findings.title: import silently mutates and discards invalid url contents, with inconsistent return and side effects
findings.body: `self.import` mutates the caller-supplied `contents` string in place via `contents << "..."` before checking url validity is already done above via early return, but note the mutation happens only after the regex check passes. More importantly, if `url` doesn't match the regex, the method returns `nil` without any error indication, silently swallowing bad data from feeds (e.g., in `poll_feed.rb` loop, a bad `url` for one item just skips that topic with no logging), making debugging feed import issues difficult.

findings.title: Unrescued exceptions in per-item processing abort the whole feed poll
findings.body: Inside `poll_feed`, `rss.items.each` calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every item without any per-item rescue. Since `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set, if any single feed item causes an exception (e.g., malformed content causing a Nokogiri parse error, or absolutize_urls raising on an invalid url), the entire job aborts, and no retry occurs, leaving all remaining feed items for that run unprocessed and silently dropped until the next hourly poll's items happen to still be present in the feed.

findings.title: feed_key method is defined but never used
findings.body: `feed_key` builds a redis key intended presumably to track feed modification/caching (likely meant to avoid refetching unchanged feeds), but it is never referenced anywhere in `poll_feed` or elsewhere in the codebase. This indicates incomplete work: the feed is always fully re-fetched and all items reprocessed every hour, which is wasteful and was presumably meant to be optimized by this key but isn't.

findings.title: No feedback given to user if embed_url is same-origin spam risk / repeated hits enqueue duplicate jobs
findings.body: Every request with no matching topic_id enqueues a `:retrieve_topic` job regardless of how recently the same `embed_url` was requested from this controller action (throttling is only applied inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which is bypassed for staff and only limited to 60 seconds otherwise). Since the controller returns the 'loading' view which polls every 30 seconds and reloads, multiple concurrent viewers of the same not-yet-imported embed URL will each enqueue a new `RetrieveTopic` job on every reload within the throttle window boundary, potentially causing bursts of duplicate job enqueues under load before the redis throttle key is set the first time (race condition between concurrent requests both checking `retrieved_recently?` before either sets the key).
